full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1998 passed by the Additional District Judge, Narsingdi in Title Appeal No. 3 of 1998 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 13-11-1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Narsingdi in Title Suit No. 29 of 1997 decreeing the suit. 

 4. The trial Court held trial of the suit upon recording of the evidence of witnesses. He decreed the suit of the plaintiff petitioner by this judgment and decree dated 13-11-97 and declared the voters list as illegal and defective. Against the said judgment and decree opposite party No. 1 as appellant preferred the Title Appeal No. 3 of 1998 in the court of the District Judge, Narsingdi. The appeal was transferred to the court of the Additional District Judge, Narsingdi who heard the same and' allowed the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The lower appellate Court dismissed the suit of the petitioner. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 31-5-1998 Passed by the Additional District Judge, Narsingdi in Title Appeal No. 3 of 1998 dismissing the suit of the petitioner after setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the petitioner moved this court under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

 8. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the aforesaid 97 persons coming as they do from different professional groups of pesh Imam. Muazzins, teachers of School and College, staff members of Medical Centre and Hospital though run by, the factory management by no stretch of imagination can be called "Workers" or "Workman" as defined in, the aforesaid 2 clauses. In support of this contention he refers to the decision reported in 18 DLR 299 in the case of Abu Bakkar Siddique vs Province of East Pakistan to show that a teacher employee is not a workman. The next submission of the learned counsel of the petitioner is that a pesh Imam or a Muazzin is not a worker within the meaning of section 2(v) of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act 1965 and in this connection he has cited a decision reported in 33 DLR 29 in the case of Manager, Shahjibazar Power Station, Bangladesh Power Development Board vs Md Gulam Hossain Khan and another. It is contended by the petitioner's learned lawyer that if a pesh Imam is not a worker within the meaning of section 2(v) of the Employment of Labour (Standing Order) Act. 1965, the Muazzin of Mosque cannot also be a worker. That an employee in a nonprofit making establishment like medical centre or hospital is not also a worker and to bring home his submission in this regard, the learned lawyer of the petitioner has referred to a citation reported in 43 DLR 655 in the case of Kumudini Hospital vs Kumudini Hospital Karmachari Union & others. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Additional Attorney-General appearing as a privately engaged counsel of opposite party No.5, submits that the above citations have no manner of application as the circumstances that have given rise to these decisions are totally different from the facts and circumstances of the instant case. To bring the pesh Imam, a Muazzin, teachers of School and College and staff members of Medical Centre and Hospital within the definition of "Worker" or "Workman" he has laid particular emphasis on the words “সারকারখানার কাজে নিয়োজিত” as mentioned in Article 4 of the Constitution of the Urea Fertilizer Factory Employees Union. It is canvassed by the learned Advocate of the opposite party No. 5 that since the pesh Imam, Muazzin, teachers of School and College and staff members of Medical Centre and Hospital of the factory are on the pay roll of the factory, they for all intents and purposes are engaged in their respective duties as workers of the factory. Next submission of the learned Advocate of the opposite party No. 5 is that the aforesaid categories of persons have been participating in elections held since long before, And no one ever challenged the propriety or legality of the voters list on the basis of which those elections were held, It is further argued by the learned Advocate for the, opposite party No. 5 that the petitioner now expressing his serious objection against the list in question kept mum at the time of its preparation. It is contended by the learned Advocate of the opposite party No. 5 that the petitioner suddenly woke up from his slumber and filed the instant suit, with a view to frustrating the election. The learned Advocate of opposite party No. 5 sums up his submissions by saying that the lower appellate" Court passed' the impugned judgment and decree quite legally and that he committed no error of law resulting in an error of decision occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the Rule obtained by the petitioner is liable to be discharged. 

 9. In the pleading, it is noticed, the petitioner has made no grievance against enlistment of staff members of Medical Centre and Hospital run by the, factory in the voters list but the trial Court has allowed, the petitioner to lead evidence in, this regard. The petitioner has taken objection to the enlistment of pesh Imam Muazzins, teachers of School and College. When this is the position it is not understood what prompted the trial Court to grant relief in favour of the petitioner declaring the entire voters list as illegal and defective. The trial Court if he found that the petitioner has been successful to prove his case in part, he ought to have given a part decree instead of striking down the entire voters list. The lower appellate Court appears to have gone to the other extreme and he set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court in its entirety holding that striking down of the voter list will create a stalemate or deadlock in the way of holding election and thereby will give rise to many complications. Both the courts below without arriving at a decision as to whether the pesh Imam, Muazzins of the Mosque, teachers" of School and College and staff members of Medical Centre and Hospital are "workers" or 'Workman" as defined in tile statutes referred to above, have handed done Judgments which are diametrically opposed to each other, the trial Court decreeing the suit and the lower appellate Court setting aside the judgment of the trial Court and dismissing the suit. 

 13. In the result the Rule is made absolute in part without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 31-5-98 passed by the Additional District Judge, Narsingdi in Title Appeal No. 3 of 1998 are hereby set aside and the appeal is sent back on remand to the lower appellate Court to deliver fresh Judgment after hearing both the parties in the light of the observations made by us in the body of this judgment. The lower appellate Court is directed to dispose of the appeal within 2(two) months from the date of receipt of the lower court records.
